title: Localizing an enriched categorical mapping cylinder retracts to its target
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences, and the fixed strict interval-attachment model $\Gamma(D,V)$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-arrow-attachment-localization], in fixed containing universes. Let $f:C\to D$ be any simplicial functor between small simplicial categories. Define $M_f$ to have the disjoint union of their object sets. Its mapping simplicial sets within the two summands are $C(x,y)$ and $D(x,y)$, respectively. For $x\in C$ and $y\in D$ put $M_f(x,y)=D(fx,y)$; for $x\in D$ and $y\in C$ put $M_f(x,y)=\varnothing$. 
Composition within a summand is its composition; for a cross arrow use $f$ on the $C$-arrow and composition in $D$. Let $j:M_f\to D$ send $x\in C$ to $fx$, act as the identity on $D$, and use $f$ on $C$-mapping sets and the identity on cross mapping sets. Let $V$ be any small set of labelled vertex arrows in $M_f$ such that $j(v)$ is an identity for every $v\in V$, and such that, for every $x\in C$, the cross arrow $x\to fx$ represented by $1_{fx}$ occurs in $V$. Then the identity-collapse extension
$$\bar j:\Gamma(M_f,V)\longrightarrow D$$
is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Neither $f$ nor the mapping simplicial sets of $C,D$ are assumed cofibrant or Kan. Empty $C$ and empty $D$ are allowed whenever the functor $f$ exists.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.6, printed pp.893--894 (PDF pp.910--911), with the fixed localization model of Notation A.3.5.1. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-category theorem.

proof.text: Write $M=M_f$ and let $i:D\to M$ be inclusion of the second summand. Its mapping maps are identities and $ji=1_D$. Define $\alpha:1_M\Rightarrow ij$ by $\alpha_x=(1_{fx}:x\to fx)$ for $x\in C$ and $\alpha_d=1_d$ for $d\in D$. This is an enriched natural transformation: on $C(x,x\prime)$ the two composites $\alpha_{x\prime}a$ and $f(a)\alpha_x$ both equal the cross simplex $f(a)$; on $D(d,d\prime)$ both equal the given simplex; on $M(x,d)=D(fx,d)$ both equal that cross simplex. For maps from the second summand to the first the domain is empty, so the naturality equation is unique. These are equalities in every simplicial degree, not merely equalities of vertex arrows. Associativity, units and commutation with simplex operators for $i,j$ and this family follow from the displayed composition formulas of the item.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.6, printed pp.893–894; the bridge natural transformation is explicit here. HTT read online at the IAS mirror, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Put $E=\Gamma(M,V)$ and denote its structure map by $q:M\to E$. The strict attachment theorem identifies $q$ with the derived localization map in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ and supplies exactly the identity-collapse extension $\bar j:E\to D$ of the statement, with $\bar j q=j$. The induced functor $\pi_0q$ inverts every labelled arrow: apply the image assertion of the localization universal property to $1_E$ and restrict it along $q$. In particular it inverts each $\alpha_x$ in the first summand, because the hypothesis puts that bridge in $V$; in the second summand $q(\alpha_d)$ is an identity. Extra labels and repeated labels impose no additional requirement here.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.6, printed pp.893–894; the bridge natural transformation is explicit here. HTT read online at the IAS mirror, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Postcompose the enriched naturality equations of Step 1 with $q$. They give a family $q(\alpha_m):q(m)\to qij(m)$ between the simplicial functors $q,qij:M\to E$. Step 2 verifies that every component is invertible in $\pi_0E$. Applying [lem-coef-simplicial-natural-equivalence-homotopy] to $A=M$, $B=E$, $F=q$ and $G=qij$ gives $[q]=[qij]$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(M,E)$. This application uses neither a Kan condition on $E$ nor a cofibrancy condition on $M$.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.6, printed pp.893–894; the bridge natural transformation is explicit here. HTT read online at the IAS mirror, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Define $s=qi:D\to E$. Strictly, $\bar j s=\bar jqi=ji=1_D$. To prove the other inverse identity in $h\mathrm{sCat}$, restrict both $s\bar j$ and $1_E$ along $q$. The resulting classes are $[qi\bar jq]=[qij]$ and $[q]$, equal by Step 3. The localization universal property, transported along the under-$M$ identification of the strict attachment theorem, says that this restriction on $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(E,E)$ is injective. Hence $[s\bar j]=[1_E]$. Thus $[s]$ is a two-sided inverse of the class of the specified $\bar j$.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.6, printed pp.893–894; the bridge natural transformation is explicit here. HTT read online at the IAS mirror, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: The last assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-target-test] says that an actual simplicial functor representing such an isomorphism is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, without local Kan or cofibrancy assumptions on its endpoints. Apply it to the isomorphism $[\bar j]$ just proved. Its essential-surjectivity condition also holds directly: every $d\in D$ is the image of $s(d)$, since $\bar j s=1_D$. This proves the required assertion about the actual identity-collapse extension. If $C$ is empty, the bridge family is empty and the same restriction argument applies with $M=D$. If $D$ is empty and $f$ exists, $C$ is empty too; no labelled vertex arrows then exist, the attaching coproduct is empty and both sides are the empty simplicial category.
